title: VBR maximum resultant force in lying positions, first post-op month (WP1, WP2)
subcategory: lying supine, prone, lateral; supine straight-leg raise
levels: L1 (VBR; fixator T12-L2 in WP1/WP2, T11-L3 in WP3)
condition: in vivo, early post-op (3-27 days), VBR + posterior fixator

quantity.name: maximum resultant force on VBR
quantity.definition: ABSOLUTE resultant force (sqrt(Fx^2+Fy^2+Fz^2)) on the telemeterised L1 VBR, in N, per patient: median (range) of the per-clip maximum (or minimum where stated) over evaluated video clips within the first post-operative month; n = number of evaluated clips. WP3 values are relative to supine rest (zero offset reset).

source.authors: Rohlmann A, Graichen F, Bender A, Kayser R, Bergmann G
source.sample: 3 patients (WP1, WP2 male; WP3 female) with telemeterised L1 VBR, first post-operative month (2-4 sessions each); in vivo, L1 compression fracture, posterior internal fixator (T12-L2 or T11-L3) + telemeterised VBR + bone graft; measured 3-27 days post-op

WP3.note: osteoporotic vertebrae; telemetry zero point changed between calibration and first measurement -> loads set to zero when lying relaxed supine (unknown offset; values are relative to supine rest)

protocol.summary: Exercises under guidance of a physiotherapist within the first post-operative month (WP1 days 4,13,20,27; WP2 days 3,13; WP3 days 4,9,16), video-synchronised telemetry; results of all sessions pooled per patient.
how_to_simulate: Place the patient model lying supine, prone or on the side, muscles relaxed
For the leg-raise row lift one straight leg while supine
Output resultant force at L1 (expected <100 N)

A whole-spine MSK model outputs total segment compression at the implant level, not the implant share; compare trends/relative changes unless the model includes the VBR and posterior fixator; whole-spine models typically predict near-zero muscle-driven compression lying, so compare order of magnitude only

WP3.note: osteoporotic vertebrae; telemetry zero point changed between calibration and first measurement -> loads set to zero when lying relaxed supine (unknown offset; values are relative to supine rest)

subject_model.source: Rohlmann 2008 Table 1 (sex, age, height, body mass, fractured vertebra, fixator level, bone graft, implantation date, sessions); days post-op from Methods 2.4

protocol.notes: Load measured on a telemeterised vertebral body replacement (modified Synex, 6 load components, accuracy ~2% force / 5% moment of 3000 N / 20 Nm calibration range) that shares the load with the posterior internal fixator, residual vertebral bone and bone graft; the VBR force is NOT the total spinal load. Pooled over all first-month sessions of a patient (median and range). Median values >400 N printed bold in the paper. Mostly maximum resultant force per clip; rows marked "MINIMUM" are minimum resultant force (Table 2 footnote b). WP3: zero point of telemetry changed, loads were set to zero lying relaxed supine (values exclude an unknown preload). Patients were not told how to perform exercises (own daily-life manner) and were under pain medication; early post-op loads vary strongly between sessions.
